<?xml version="1.0"?><rss version="2.0"><channel><title>Henry Sheldon Museum</title><item><title>Walking Tour of Middlebury</title><link>https://www.henrysheldonmuseum.org/events/walking-tour-of-middlebury-dznga-zjm2n-kwzax</link><guid isPermaLink="false">5e7a0da508e4e2019ee23004:5e7a1ad5276db47ef00cb29a:69d692a65911cc6417657502</guid><description><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class="">Learn about the history of Middlebury with a 60-minute, 1-mile narrated walking tour. Follow Todd Goodyear as he weaves through town and time - from the 1780’s to the 1980’s - spotlighting the people who helped shape Middlebury’s character. You’ll learn about Painter and Foote, the influential Battell and Ilsley families, Charles Mraz the bee man, and even Bud the barber. Whether you’re a curious visitor or a lifelong local, you’ll leave seeing Middlebury in a whole new light.</p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class="">The tour departs from the Henry Sheldon Museum and is a 1 mile walking loop. Tickets are $20 for adults and $12 for 13 &amp; under.  Your ticket includes admission to the Museum that day.</p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class=""><strong>About Todd Goodyear</strong>: Todd has spent his entire life in Addison County and now lives in&nbsp;Middlebury. Todd has a lifelong love of history and a passion for exploring the stories that make our town unique. In his free time, you’ll often find him in museums, libraries, or strolling Middlebury’s streets, pausing at historical markers to uncover the past!</p>

  </a></description></item><item><title>Pins and Pies, Linens and Lamps: Imagining the World of Charity & Sylvia</title><link>https://www.henrysheldonmuseum.org/events/pins-and-pies-linens-and-lamps-imagining-the-world-of-charity-sylvia</link><guid isPermaLink="false">5e7a0da508e4e2019ee23004:5e7a1ad5276db47ef00cb29a:6abfd375557a237b88f44e21</guid><description><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The publication of Tillie Walden’s recent graphic novel Charity &amp; Sylvia–and its selection as the 2026 “Vermont Reads”–was a wonderful impetus for the Henry Sheldon Museum to rethink how we might feature the story of Charity Bryant and Sylvia Drake in the museum galleries. While we’ve long treasured the Charity and Sylvia archives– their letters, poems, diaries, and the like– their story hasn’t been visible in the museum itself. In curating Drawing on the Archive, we built a collaborative curatorial team where Tillie Walden’s contemporary illustrations could converse with 19th century objects and archival materials, and interpretation was shared among museum staff and community curators.</p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Henry Sheldon Museum Executive Director Coco Moseley and Middlebury College Associate Professor Ellery Foutch share their stories behind the making of the new exhibition “Drawing on the Archive: Tillie Walden’s Charity &amp; Sylvia.”</p><h4 data-rte-preserve-empty="true"><strong>About the presenters</strong></h4><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Coco Moseley is the Executive Director of the <a href="https://www.henrysheldonmuseum.org/">Henry Sheldon Museum</a> in Middlebury. Since beginning this role in 2023, she has worked alongside the staff, board and community to reimagine the Sheldon Museum as a place where stories, history and art can inspire visitors today.</p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Ellery Foutch is an Associate Professor in the American Studies Program at Middlebury College, where she teaches classes on the art and material culture of the United States, as well as critical museum studies.   <p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class=""></p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class=""></p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class="">Join us for an embroidery workshop with  Eman Hayyat. Eman grew up in Middlebury, VT to a Palestinian/Jordanian family. She spent her summers in Jordan which strengthened her ties to the culture of the region. Hayyat’s travels influenced her decision to pursue a degree in Global and Middle Eastern Studies and work in a field that allows her to interact with many different cultures. Hayyat is particularly drawn to traditional art forms, such as dance, music , cooking and most recently, Tatreez. She enjoys creating things that can be enjoyed by many, be it a meal that can be shared with friends and family or a newly completed Tatreez project that can be displayed as a symbol of her heritage.</p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class=""></p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class="">This workshop anticipates a permanent immigration history exhibit in 2027. Participants will learn a traditional Palestinian embroidery pattern and have the opportunity to think about, share, and discuss how and why immigrants to Vermont bring traditional art-making and decorative practices with them. </p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class=""></p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class="">This event is made possible with generous support from a <a target="_blank" href="https://vermonthistory.org/vermont-community-immigration-history-grants">Vermont Community Immigration History</a> grant funded by the <a target="_blank" href="https://www.lostmural.org/">Lost Mural Project</a> and administered by the <a target="_blank" href="https://vermonthistory.org/">Vermont Historical Society</a>.</p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class=""></p><p data-rte-preserve-empty="true" class="">Space for this workshop is limited. Ages 16 and up. *Due to overwhelming interest, the workshop is now full. Please join the waitlist below and we will contact you if a space open up.
